audits.title: An audit of current practice and management of metastatic spinal cord compression at a regional cancer centre.
audits.standard: NICE guidance on metastatic spinal cord compression

cycle1.result: 5 (50%) had MRI within 24 hours; 6 (60%) had full MRI scan; 8 (80%) had corticosteroids before MRI; 6 (60%) had radiotherapy within 24 hours; 4 (40%) referred to orthopaedics

audits.other_findings: Number unable to walk increased by 20% up to 14 days after confirmation; authors recommend a fast-track referral pathway and education.
audits.citation: Sui J, Fleming JS, Kehoe M. An audit of current practice and management of metastatic spinal cord compression at a regional cancer centre. Ir Med J. 2011;104(4):111-114. PMID: 21675093.

audits.title: The British Orthopaedic Oncology Management (BOOM) audit.
audits.standard: BOOS/BOA guidelines for metastatic bone disease
audits.setting: 84 UK hospitals, trainee-led national collaborative audit (BOOM)

cycle1.result: No designated MBD lead in 39% of centres (33/84); inadequate radiographs in 19% (160/846); no up-to-date staging CT in 29% (247/846); oncology opinion 69% (584/846); prognosis estimation 38% (223/846).

audits.other_findings: Of 215 patients with a solitary metastasis, tertiary MBD centre opinion and biopsy were sought in 60% (130/215); surgery in 38% (319/846).
audits.citation: Archer JE, Chauhan GS, Dewan V, Osman K, Thomson C, Nandra RS, et al.. The British Orthopaedic Oncology Management (BOOM) audit. Bone Joint J. 2023;105-B(10):1115-1122. doi:10.1302/0301-620x.105b10.bjj-2023-0443.r1. PMID: 37777202.

audits.title: 115 An Audit on Dexamethasone Prescribing Practice on Surgically Managed Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression Patients in the Manchester Centre for Clinical Neurosciences: Lessons Learned in Closing the Loop
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and Edinburgh/Christie's guidelines for steroid loading dose (16 mg) and weaning
audits.setting: Tertiary spinal unit, Manchester Centre for Clinical Neurosciences, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 1/33 received correct 16 mg loading dose; 27 went straight to 8 mg BD; 5 received no dexamethasone; 26 weaned accordingly; 38% correctly weaned (as later compared).

cycle2.result: 93% correctly weaned compared with 38% previously; almost all still did not receive the correct loading dose.

audits.other_findings: Loading dose prescribing remained poor despite appropriate maintenance dosing.
audits.citation: Laurente R, Mohammed R, Elmalky M. 115 An Audit on Dexamethasone Prescribing Practice on Surgically Managed Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression Patients in the Manchester Centre for Clinical Neurosciences: Lessons Learned in Closing the Loop. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.370.

audits.title: A royal college of radiologists national audit of radiotherapy in the treatment of metastatic spinal cord compression and implications for the development of acute oncology services.
audits.standard: National standards for metastatic spinal cord compression management
audits.setting: UK cancer centres (Royal College of Radiologists national audit)

cycle1.result: 93% (358) had MRI within 24 h of referral; 111 (32%) good prognosis patients discussed with spinal surgeons, 10 proceeded to surgery; 69% of paraplegic patients received multiple fractions.

cycle2.result: 205 (97%) had MRI within 24 h; 94 (41%) good prognosis patients discussed with surgeons, 9 proceeded to surgery; 62% of paraplegic patients received more than a single fraction.

audits.other_findings: An MSCC co-ordinator was available in 164/323 cases and involved in management in 26% in 2012. Centres: 42 (74%) in 2008, 52 (90%) in 2012.
audits.citation: McGivern UM, Drinkwater KJ, Clarke JI, Locke I. A royal college of radiologists national audit of radiotherapy in the treatment of metastatic spinal cord compression and implications for the development of acute oncology services. Clin Oncol (R Coll Radiol). 2014;26(8):453-460. doi:10.1016/j.clon.2014.04.032. PMID: 24933650.

audits.title: Spinal MRI in Patients with Suspected Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression: A Quality Improvement Audit in a District General Hospital in Kent, UK.
audits.standard: NICE: whole-spine MRI within 24 h for back pain with neurological signs or symptoms
audits.setting: Medway Maritime Hospital (district general hospital), Kent

cycle1.result: MRI within 24 h in 43/69 (62%); 16 of 25 delayed cases waited more than 48 h.

audits.intervention: Informational flyers and regular MSCC training, including trainee teaching and grand round presentations.
audits.other_findings: Main reasons for delay were patient compliance and pain control; steroid timing was also recorded.
audits.citation: Bachour ME, Rabbani RD, Hasan MR, Akter S, Chilakuluri P, Banerjee S, et al.. Spinal MRI in Patients with Suspected Metastatic Spinal Cord Compression: A Quality Improvement Audit in a District General Hospital in Kent, UK. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2025;22(3):401. doi:10.3390/ijerph22030401. PMID: 40238444.

audits.title: MANAGEMENT OF METASTATIC SPINAL CORD COMPRESSION: AUDIT
audits.standard: NICE guidance on MSCC (MRI within 24 hours target 100%)

cycle1.result: Only 53% of suspected MSCC patients had MRI within 24 hours; two thirds had radiotherapy within one day; LMWH and analgesia given in 96%; all received steroids but dexamethasone prescribing inconsistent.

audits.other_findings: Three month survival 56%; staff education and a local protocol recommended with re-audit after 6 to 12 months.
audits.citation: Hanchanale S, Neoh K, Waldock J, Lenton J, Naik J. MANAGEMENT OF METASTATIC SPINAL CORD COMPRESSION: AUDIT. BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care. 2014;4(Suppl 1):A54.2-A54. doi:10.1136/bmjspcare-2014-000654.154.
